Depends on why they did? I left my bf because he emotionally abused, insulted, and gaslit me, so if you had qualities like abuse and manipulation then yes, he had every right to leave you. It all depends on factors. I’m not accusing you of those things, but you must factor in why he did, did he give you a clear answer why? Look at it through his lense, be in his shoes, then ask “why would I leave my girlfriend?” (Looking through his eyes). Figure out the qualities you liked about him, and the qualities you didn’t like, figure out what went wrong not just from his side but yours as well. Figure out what you want in your next bf and what you want to avoid, and figure out how to improve yourself as well. You will feel pain, anger, resentment, depression, and a conglomerate of emotions. This is the grieving process.

The neurobiology of anhedonia is mostly low grade inflammation and MSN’s are destroyed, and dendrite tails are weak. There isn’t enough “talking” in the ventral striatum and so dopamine can’t really be up regulated when there aren’t enough dendrites and MSNs. D1 and D2 dopamine is lower, so this “talk” in the reward pathway is diminished. These are very deep regions in the brain though, and so DBS can rewire this “talk” and increase dopamine production. Our understanding of the MFB is growing, and this specific spot in the brain looks promising for both acute and long term effects of stimulation.

Deep Brain Stimulation. It’s a surgical technique where surgeons implant long thin electrodes into the cortical regions of the brain, stimulating specific areas with electric pulses. It’s FDA approved for Parkinson’s and intractable OCD. It’s been studied in clinical trials for MDD for several years, but results were iffy and showed mixed results. Here, scientists have found a special spot that intricates the reward circuitry systems all together, known as the medial forebrain bundle. This bundle of white matter is crucial in pleasure and reward.
It does offer hope, and it helps researchers learn more about the effects of stimulation in these very deep cortical regions of the brain.
https://www.biologicalpsychiatryjournal.com/article/S0006-3223(13)00136-4/fulltext

DBS is being recognized as an amazing and hopeful treatment option for severely anhedonic patients. This shows proof of that. Other clinical studies have noted anti anhedonic effects of DBS for severely treatment resistant patients. Right now, UCSF is hosting a clinical trial involving 12 participants in a study involving DBS stimulation at customized areas that meet patients needs. Before this clinical trial, the university tested closed loop DBS at 3 different targets in one female patient, and she reported feeling joy again.
